deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page is a very faint, heavily cancelled pencil draft written over a printed postal-ledger form ('No 10', columns Auslage / Porto / Franko). The previous and next folios are drafts on cross-cuts (Querschnitte) of n-fold connected surfaces. This folio is a draft of the preparatory section of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), the part headed 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs für die Theorie der Integrale von zweigliedrigen vollständigen Differentialien'. Little can be read with certainty. The legible fragments are: '..., daß ... X dx + Y dy ein vollständiges Differential ...', '... ∫ X dx + Y dy ...', '... gegen diese ... in derselben Richtung ...', a cancelled parenthesis with (∂X/∂y − ∂Y/∂x) near the top right, 'vollständig ...', '... a und b ...', '... die ganze Begrenzung ...', and near the bottom '... vollständige Begrenzung ... eines Theils ...'. From these fragments and the published text, the content is the following.

(1) Setting. X and Y are continuous functions of position on a surface T spread over the (x,y)-plane. By Green's theorem, ∫_{∂S}(X dx + Y dy) = ∬_S (∂Y/∂x − ∂X/∂y) dx dy, with the boundary of S traversed in the positive sense relative to S. So if ∂X/∂y − ∂Y/∂x = 0 throughout S, then ∫(X dx + Y dy) over the whole boundary of S is 0. Equivalently, X dx + Y dy is then a complete (exact) differential locally.

(2) Consequence for curves. If two curves a and b together form the complete boundary of a part of T, the integral along a equals the integral along b, both taken in the same direction (presumably the phrase 'in derselben Richtung'). Hence the integral from a fixed point to a variable point is path-independent on a simply connected surface.

(3) Multiply connected case. On a multiply connected T the integral may have constant 'periods' across the cross-cuts. The next folio develops this: an n-fold connected surface becomes simply connected after n−1 cuts.

All formulas beyond the readable fragments are my reconstruction from the published 1857 text. The page contains no computation beyond these statements.
errors: No mathematical errors are detectable. The text is largely illegible and cancelled, so its correctness cannot be checked in detail.

results.what: Integral of X dx + Y dy over the whole boundary vanishes when ∂X/∂y = ∂Y/∂x (via the double-integral identity)
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / closedness implies local exactness
results.usually_credited_to: Green 1828, Gauss, Cauchy; this form appears in Riemann's 1851 dissertation and in the 1857 Abelian functions paper

results.what: Equality of integrals along curves a and b that together bound a region; periods on multiply connected surfaces
results.modern_name: Homology invariance of integrals of closed 1-forms / de Rham periods

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material Riemann published in 1857 (Crelle 54, analysis situs lemmas), and it is well known as his.
